title: Heaps and priority queues
summary: Always get the smallest (or largest) next, in O(log n): priority queues, Top K and k-way merges.

questions.prompt: You keep the k largest of n numbers with a min-heap that never holds more than k elements. What is the time complexity?
To keep the k largest numbers seen so far, which heap do you use and why?
options: A min-heap of size k: its smallest element is the one to evict when a larger number arrives
A max-heap of size k, evicting its largest
A sorted array, re-sorted after every number

questions.prompt: True or false: iterating over a PriorityQueue with a for-each loop visits the elements in priority order.
Merge k sorted lists into one sorted list. Which approach?
options: A min-heap holding the current first element of each list
Scan all k list heads to find the smallest, every time
